stem: What is the detrimental effect of 'Multipath Fading' in RF wireless communications, and how does modern 802.11 MIMO technology leverage it?
explanation: Multipath fading occurs when radio signals reflect off walls and obstacles, arriving at the receiver slightly out of phase and causing destructive interference. MIMO uses multiple antennas and spatial multiplexing to recombine these multipath signals, increasing throughput instead of suffering degradation.

choices.text: Reflected signals arrive out of phase causing destructive fading; MIMO uses spatial multiplexing across multiple antennas to recombine these signals for higher throughput
Multipath fading burns out the RF transmitter; MIMO adds a liquid cooling circuit to the AP
Multipath fading shifts frequencies into the infrared band; MIMO converts radio signals into visible light
Multipath fading drains client battery power; MIMO disables 5 GHz radios when roaming

stem: In RF power mathematics, what is the 'Rule of 10s and 3s' when calculating signal gains and losses in dBm?
explanation: In RF math: +3 dB doubles power (x2), -3 dB halves power (/2); +10 dB multiplies power by 10 (x10), and -10 dB divides power by 10 (/10).

choices.text: +3 dB doubles power, -3 dB halves power; +10 dB multiplies power by 10, -10 dB divides power by 10
+3 dB adds 3 milliwatts, +10 dB adds 10 milliwatts
+3 dB triples the frequency, +10 dB increases frequency tenfold
+3 dB adds 3 channels, +10 dB increases antenna length by 10 cm

stem: What is the primary architectural requirement for installing Plenum-rated (CMP) Ethernet cabling instead of Riser-rated (CMR) cabling?
explanation: Plenum cabling has a special fire-retardant jacket (such as FEP) that emits low smoke and non-toxic fumes when burning. Building codes mandate its use in air-handling plenum spaces (such as drop ceilings and raised floors) used for building HVAC circulation.

choices.text: It is coated with fire-retardant materials that emit low smoke and non-toxic fumes, required in HVAC air-handling spaces
It supports higher transmission bandwidth up to 100 Gbps
It contains internal copper shielding against underwater submersion
It is required strictly for vertical risers between elevator shafts

stem: What is 'Alien Crosstalk' (AXT) in high-speed twisted-pair copper cabling, and which category standard was designed specifically to suppress it for 10GBASE-T?
explanation: Alien Crosstalk is electromagnetic noise coupled between adjacent, parallel cables bundled together in a conduit or tray. Category 6A (Cat 6A) was specifically engineered with improved internal shielding and tighter pair twists to eliminate AXT up to 500 MHz for 100-meter 10GBASE-T.

choices.text: Electromagnetic interference coupled between adjacent cables in a bundle; Category 6A was engineered to eliminate it for 10GBASE-T
Radio interference from extraterrestrial satellite transmissions; Category 5e was designed to block it
Signal leakage into single-mode optical fiber cores; Category 7 blocks it
Electrical voltage spikes from PoE injectors; Category 3 suppresses it

stem: In a classical three-tier hierarchical campus network design, what is the primary role of the Access Layer?
explanation: The Access layer directly attaches end-user endpoints (PCs, printers, IP phones, wireless access points) to the enterprise network and enforces port-level security and VLAN membership.

choices.text: Directly connecting end-user endpoints, IP phones, and wireless APs to the network and enforcing port security
Providing high-speed non-blocking backbone packet transport between campus buildings
Connecting the enterprise to external Internet Service Providers via BGP
Hosting centralized enterprise data center database servers

stem: What is Cisco StackWise technology, and what operational advantage does it deliver at the campus Access Layer?
explanation: Cisco StackWise allows multiple physical Catalyst switches to be cabled together via specialized high-speed backplane cables, operating as a single unified logical switch with a shared control plane, single management IP, and aggregated bandwidth.

choices.text: Interconnects multiple physical switches into a single logical switch with unified management and a shared backplane
Converts Ethernet switches into cellular 5G base stations
Automatically backs up running configuration files to external floppy disks
Enables Layer 2 frame switching without requiring physical cabling

stem: Which standard command-line diagnostic tool transmits ICMP Echo Requests to verify Layer 3 IP reachability to a remote host?
explanation: The `ping` utility transmits ICMP Type 8 (Echo Request) packets and listens for ICMP Type 0 (Echo Reply) packets to confirm basic IP connectivity and calculate round-trip latency.

choices.text: ping
traceroute
netstat
arp -a

stem: How does the 'traceroute' (or 'tracert') diagnostic command discover and display each intermediate router hop along a path to a destination?
explanation: Traceroute sends packets with incrementally increasing Time to Live (TTL) values, starting at TTL=1. Each intermediate router decrements TTL to 0, drops the packet, and returns an ICMP Time Exceeded message, revealing its IP address.

choices.text: It transmits packets with incrementally increasing TTL values, recording the source IP of received ICMP Time Exceeded messages
It queries the DNS root servers for the physical geographic location of each router
It broadcasts ARP requests across each intermediate WAN link
It negotiates BGP peering sessions with each router along the path

stem: How many usable host IP addresses are available in a subnet configured with a /29 subnet mask (255.255.255.248)?
explanation: A /29 mask leaves 32 - 29 = 3 host bits. Total addresses = 2^3 = 8. Subtracting network ID and broadcast yields 8 - 2 = 6 usable host addresses.

stem: An organization is assigned the network block 198.51.100.0/24 and needs to create at least 10 subnets, each supporting at least 12 usable hosts. What subnet mask should be configured?
explanation: Borrowing 4 host bits gives 2^4 = 16 subnets (meeting >= 10 requirement). With 4 host bits remaining (32 - 28 = 4), each subnet supports 2^4 - 2 = 14 usable hosts (meeting >= 12 requirement). The mask is /28 (255.255.255.240).

stem: How many total bits make up an IPv6 address, and how are they represented in textual human-readable format?
explanation: An IPv6 address is 128 bits in length, represented as 8 groups of 4 hexadecimal digits (16 bits per group) separated by colons.

choices.text: 128 bits, represented as 8 groups of 4 hexadecimal digits separated by colons
32 bits, represented as 4 decimal octets separated by dots
64 bits, represented as 8 octets separated by hyphens
256 bits, represented as 16 pairs of hex digits

stem: In standard IPv6 Global Unicast Address (GUA) architecture, what are the three hierarchical structural components that comprise the 128-bit address?
explanation: A standard IPv6 GUA consists of: a Global Routing Prefix (typically /48 assigned by RIR/ISP), a Subnet ID (16 bits assigned by the enterprise), and a 64-bit Interface ID identifying the host.

choices.text: Global Routing Prefix, Subnet ID, and Interface ID
Network Class, Host ID, and Port Number
Autonomous System Number, BGP Weight, and MAC Address
VLAN ID, OSPF Process ID, and Tunnel Tag

stem: Which networking components operate primarily at Layer 1 (Physical layer) of the OSI reference model?
explanation: The Physical layer encompasses raw bit transmission across physical media, including copper cables (Cat 6), optical fibers, RJ-45/LC connectors, patch panels, repeaters, and transceiver optics.

choices.text: Cabling, transceivers, connectors, and physical repeaters
Network switches and network interface cards
IP routers and Layer 3 multilayer switches
Web Application Firewalls and proxy servers

stem: At which layer of the OSI model does a protocol establish end-to-end flow control using sliding windows, acknowledgments, and sequence numbers?
explanation: The Transport Layer (Layer 4) provides transparent, reliable data transfer between end systems, managing flow control (sliding window), error recovery, and segmentation (TCP).

choices.text: Transport Layer (Layer 4)
Network Layer (Layer 3)
Data Link Layer (Layer 2)
Session Layer (Layer 5)

stem: What is the primary security objective of deploying a Virtual Private Network (VPN) gateway appliance?
explanation: A VPN gateway encrypts traffic traversing public or untrusted networks (such as the Internet), ensuring data confidentiality, integrity, and endpoint authentication.

choices.text: Establishing encrypted tunnels across untrusted public networks to provide data confidentiality and integrity
Filtering spam and phishing emails from corporate mailboxes
Generating dynamic IP addresses for local LAN clients
Preventing physical lightning surges from entering data center racks

stem: What is the primary role of a Forward Proxy server in an enterprise corporate network?
explanation: A Forward Proxy sits between internal client workstations and the public Internet. It intercepts outbound web requests to enforce corporate acceptable use policies, perform malware and URL filtering, cache web pages, and mask internal IP addresses.

choices.text: Intermediates outbound web requests from internal clients to external servers for policy enforcement, content filtering, and caching
Terminates inbound customer connections to protect public-facing web servers
Assigns dynamic IP addresses to internal network switches via DHCP
Routes BGP traffic between external autonomous systems

stem: In hypervisor virtualization, what is a VMware vSphere Distributed Switch (vDS) and how does it improve upon a Standard vSwitch?
explanation: A Distributed Switch functions as a single unified virtual switch spanning across all hypervisors in a cluster, managed centrally by vCenter. This eliminates the need to configure vSwitches and port groups individually on each physical host.

choices.text: Centralizes virtual switch administration across all clustered hosts, providing consistent port group configurations and network policies
Routes IP packets without requiring an IP default gateway
Replaces physical server network cards with optical wireless transceivers
Enables virtual machines to bypass 802.1Q VLAN encapsulation completely

stem: Can two virtual machines attached to different VLANs on the same hypervisor virtual switch (vSwitch) communicate directly without a Layer 3 routing device?
explanation: No. A virtual switch enforces Layer 2 VLAN isolation identically to a physical switch. Traffic between different VLANs must be routed by an external router or a Layer 3 multilayer switch/virtual router.

choices.text: No, inter-VLAN traffic must be routed by an external router or Layer 3 switch
Yes, because all virtual machines share the same host physical RAM
Yes, by configuring both VMs with the same MAC address
Yes, provided the virtual switch is running in transparent mode

stem: Which Cisco IOS switchport command statically configures an interface into permanent trunking mode, regardless of neighbor negotiation?
explanation: The command `switchport mode trunk` forces the interface into permanent 802.1Q trunking mode, converting the link to a trunk even if the neighbor does not initiate negotiation.

choices.text: switchport mode trunk
switchport trunk enable
switchport mode dynamic desirable
switchport negotiate trunk

stem: What operational link state results if Switch A's interface is configured with 'switchport mode dynamic desirable' and connecting Switch B's interface is configured with 'switchport mode access'?
explanation: Because Switch B is explicitly fixed in access mode, it will reject any DTP trunk negotiation attempts initiated by Switch A's `dynamic desirable` configuration. Consequently, the link operates as an Access port.

choices.text: The link operates as an access link
The link operates as an 802.1Q trunk link
Both ports enter an err-disabled mismatch state
The link shuts down due to a BPDU guard violation

stem: What essential neighbor information is displayed in the output of the 'show cdp neighbors' command on a Cisco switch?
explanation: `show cdp neighbors` displays the neighbor Device ID (hostname), local interface, holdtime, capabilities (router, switch), platform (hardware model), and remote port ID.

choices.text: Neighbor Device ID, local interface, holdtime, capabilities, hardware platform, and remote port ID
IP routing table entries, administrative distance, and metric costs
Password hashes and secret keys configured on the remote device
Dynamic ARP cache bindings and DHCP lease durations

stem: If Link Layer Discovery Protocol (LLDP) has been disabled on a specific switch interface, which two commands are used to re-enable both LLDP transmission and reception?
explanation: Under interface configuration mode, entering `lldp transmit` enables the port to send LLDP advertisements, and `lldp receive` enables the port to process incoming LLDP advertisements.

choices.text: lldp transmit and lldp receive
lldp enable both
switchport lldp on
service lldp start

stem: Which Cisco IOS command displays only the statically configured MAC address entries in a switch's CAM table?
explanation: The command `show mac address-table static` lists all statically configured MAC address table entries, including system-reserved addresses and secure sticky addresses.

choices.text: show mac address-table static
show static mac-table
show mac address-table dynamic
show cam table static-only

stem: What action does an Ethernet switch take when it receives a unicast frame whose destination MAC address is NOT found in its MAC address table?
explanation: This condition is known as an 'unknown unicast' frame. The switch floods the frame out all active interfaces assigned to the same VLAN, except the interface on which the frame was received.

choices.text: It floods the frame out all active ports in the same VLAN except the receiving ingress port
It immediately discards the frame and sends an ICMP Host Unreachable message
It forwards the frame exclusively to the Spanning Tree root bridge
It holds the frame in RAM buffer for 300 seconds until an ARP reply is received

stem: Under the original IEEE 802.3af (PoE) standard, what is the maximum power allocated by Power Sourcing Equipment (PSE) per switch port?
explanation: Under IEEE 802.3af, the PSE delivers up to 15.4 Watts of DC power (guaranteeing 12.95 Watts at the powered device over 100 meters of cabling).

choices.text: 15.4 Watts
30.0 Watts
60.0 Watts
7.0 Watts

stem: In Power over Ethernet (PoE) architecture, what is a Powered Device (PD)?
explanation: A Powered Device (PD) is any network endpoint that receives electrical power over the twisted-pair Ethernet cable from Power Sourcing Equipment (such as an IP phone, wireless AP, or PTZ camera).

choices.text: A network endpoint (such as an IP phone or wireless AP) that draws its electrical power over the Ethernet cable from a PSE
A redundant backup power supply installed in a switch chassis
A diesel generator providing emergency building power
An optical transceiver module drawing power from fiber light pulses

stem: What is the default violation action executed on a Cisco switch port if Port Security is enabled without specifying an explicit violation mode?
explanation: If no mode is specified (`switchport port-security violation`), Cisco IOS defaults to `shutdown` mode, which immediately err-disables the interface upon detecting an unauthorized MAC.

choices.text: shutdown
restrict
protect
errdisable-log

stem: What operational state does a switch port transition into when an unauthorized device triggers a Port Security violation under 'shutdown' mode?
explanation: The switch immediately disables the interface and places it into the `down / down (err-disabled)` state, turning the physical port LED amber and sending an SNMP trap and syslog message.

choices.text: The port is shut down and placed into the err-disabled state, turning the port LED amber
The port remains up, but all frames are forwarded to the SPAN destination port
The port transitions to a half-duplex 10 Mbps access port
The port continues forwarding frames but sends warning emails to the administrator

stem: Which IEEE standard replaced legacy 802.1D Spanning Tree to deliver rapid convergence within a few hundred milliseconds?
explanation: IEEE 802.1w defines Rapid Spanning Tree Protocol (RSTP), reducing topology convergence times from 30–50 seconds down to sub-second speeds.

choices.text: IEEE 802.1w
IEEE 802.1Q
IEEE 802.1X
IEEE 802.3ad

stem: How does Rapid Spanning Tree Protocol (RSTP / 802.1w) achieve rapid convergence without relying on legacy forward delay timers?
explanation: RSTP uses an active handshake mechanism known as the Proposal and Agreement sequence across point-to-point links, allowing ports to transition directly to Forwarding as soon as the neighboring switch agrees.

choices.text: Through an explicit Proposal and Agreement handshake exchange across point-to-point links
By reducing the 802.1D listening and learning timers to 1 second each
By using RIP routing updates to determine bridge topology
By disabling STP root bridge elections completely

stem: Which three categories of Layer 2 traffic can be independently monitored and suppressed by Cisco Storm Control?
explanation: Storm Control can monitor and rate-limit: 1) Broadcast traffic, 2) Multicast traffic, and 3) Unknown Unicast traffic.

choices.text: Broadcast, Multicast, and Unknown Unicast
Known Unicast, TCP, and UDP
ICMP, OSPF, and BGP
Voice VLAN, Data VLAN, and Native VLAN

stem: What is a 'Switch Spoofing' VLAN hopping attack, and what configuration best-practice prevents it on access ports?
explanation: In switch spoofing, an attacker sends DTP negotiation frames pretending to be a switch to form a trunk link, thereby gaining access to all VLANs. Best practice is to statically configure access ports (`switchport mode access`) and disable DTP with `switchport nonegotiate`.

choices.text: An attacker sends DTP frames to negotiate an unauthorized trunk; prevented by configuring 'switchport mode access' and 'switchport nonegotiate'
An attacker overflows the MAC table; prevented by enabling BPDU Guard
An attacker alters the native VLAN ID; prevented by enabling VTP pruning
An attacker floods ARP requests; prevented by configuring port security sticky

stem: What is a 'Fully Specified' static route in Cisco IOS?
explanation: A fully specified static route explicitly identifies both the local outgoing exit interface and the next-hop IP address (e.g. `ip route 10.1.1.0 255.255.255.0 GigabitEthernet0/1 192.168.1.2`).

choices.text: A static route that specifies both the outgoing exit interface and the next-hop IP address
A static route that points exclusively to the loopback interface
A static route that dynamically tracks interface line protocol via IP SLA
A static route that has an administrative distance of 1

stem: Why is specifying the local exit interface mandatory when configuring an IPv6 static route using a Link-Local address (FE80::/10) as the next hop?
explanation: Because Link-Local addresses are link-scoped and not globally unique, the exact same link-local address can exist on multiple adjacent neighbors across different router interfaces. Specifying the exit interface resolves the link ambiguity.

choices.text: Because Link-Local addresses are link-scoped and ambiguous without an explicit local outgoing interface
Because Link-Local addresses cannot be processed by hardware CEF tables
Because IPv6 static routes fail without an active OSPFv3 process
Because Link-Local addresses are automatically translated via NAT-PT

stem: Which command entered under 'router ospf 1' activates OSPF on all interfaces belonging to subnet 10.0.0.0/8 and assigns them to Area 0?
explanation: The command `network 10.0.0.0 0.255.255.255 area 0` matches any interface with an IP address starting with 10.x.x.x and includes it in OSPF Area 0.

choices.text: ip ospf 10.0.0.0 area 0
router-area 0 network 10.0.0.0/8

stem: What is the modern Cisco IOS command to activate OSPF directly on interface GigabitEthernet0/1 for process ID 10 and Area 0, without using the global 'network' statement?
explanation: In modern Cisco IOS, OSPF can be enabled directly under the interface with `ip ospf 10 area 0`, which is more explicit and less error-prone than wildcard mask network statements.

choices.text: ip ospf 10 area 0 (entered under interface configuration mode)
enable ospf 10 area 0
ospf process 10 area 0 activate
ip routing ospf 10 area 0

stem: In which OSPF neighbor state is the Designated Router (DR) and Backup Designated Router (BDR) election completed on a broadcast multi-access Ethernet network?
explanation: DR/BDR elections occur during the 2-Way state, once bidirectional communication has been confirmed by examining neighbor lists in Hello packets.

choices.text: 2-Way state
Init state
ExStart state
Full state

stem: What is the final stable operational state achieved between two adjacent OSPF routers when their Link-State Databases are fully synchronized?
explanation: The Full state indicates that neighbor routers are fully adjacent and their Link-State Databases (LSDBs) are identical and completely synchronized.

choices.text: Full state
Loading state
Exchange state
2-Way state

stem: What are the default OSPF Hello and Dead timer intervals on a Non-Broadcast Multi-Access (NBMA) network?
explanation: On NBMA networks (and point-to-multipoint non-broadcast), OSPF uses a 30-second Hello interval and a 120-second Dead interval.

choices.text: Hello: 30 seconds; Dead: 120 seconds
Hello: 10 seconds; Dead: 40 seconds
Hello: 5 seconds; Dead: 15 seconds
Hello: 60 seconds; Dead: 180 seconds

stem: Which interface configuration command configures an Ethernet interface to operate as an OSPF point-to-point network, eliminating the overhead of DR/BDR elections?
explanation: The command `ip ospf network point-to-point` changes the OSPF network type from broadcast to point-to-point, removing the requirement for DR/BDR elections and speeding up convergence.

choices.text: ip ospf network point-to-point
ospf mode p2p
no ospf dr-election
ip ospf neighbor-mode direct

stem: Which mathematical algorithm is used by OSPF to calculate the shortest loop-free path to every destination prefix in the network?
explanation: OSPF uses Dijkstra's Shortest Path First (SPF) algorithm to calculate loop-free paths through the network topology.

choices.text: Dijkstra's Shortest Path First (SPF) algorithm
Diffusing Update Algorithm (DUAL)
Bellman-Ford distance-vector algorithm
Spanning Tree Algorithm (STA)

stem: What type of packet does an OSPF router send periodically to discover neighboring routers and verify their reachability?
explanation: OSPF Hello packets are sent periodically out all OSPF-enabled interfaces to discover neighbors, negotiate parameters, and serve as keepalives.

choices.text: Hello packet
Database Description (DBD) packet
Link-State Request (LSR) packet
Link-State Update (LSU) packet

stem: An engineer notices that an OSPF neighbor adjacency is flapping repeatedly between FULL and DOWN. What physical layer or data link issue is a common root cause?
explanation: Duplex mismatches, intermittent physical cabling faults, dirty fiber optics, or an unstable point-to-point wireless bridge frequently cause dropped Hellos or corrupted DBD/LSU packets, resulting in OSPF adjacency flapping.

choices.text: A physical cable fault, dirty optical connector, or duplex mismatch causing packet drops and missed Hellos
An OSPF reference bandwidth mismatch between core routers
The router having an odd-numbered loopback IP address
The use of an excessive number of standard ACL statements

stem: Which Cisco IOS privileged exec command provides a summary list of all active OSPF neighbors, their state, and neighbor interface IP addresses?
explanation: The command `show ip ospf neighbor` displays neighbor router IDs, priority, state (e.g. FULL/DROTHER, 2-WAY), dead timer countdown, address, and local interface.

choices.text: show ip ospf neighbor
show ospf adjacencies
show ip route ospf-neighbors
show ip protocols neighbors

stem: In modern Cisco IOS-XE, how can a single OSPFv3 routing process be configured to support both IPv4 and IPv6 address families concurrently?
explanation: OSPFv3 supports multi-address families using the `address-family` configuration mode (e.g. `address-family ipv4 unicast` and `address-family ipv6 unicast`), allowing both protocol families to run inside a single unified OSPFv3 process.

choices.text: Through OSPFv3 Address Families ('address-family ipv4 unicast' and 'address-family ipv6 unicast')
By configuring OSPFv2 with 128-bit wildcard masks
By encapsulating OSPFv2 inside GRE tunnels across IPv6 interfaces
By enabling BGP multiprotocol extensions

stem: What is the purpose of the 'Gateway of Last Resort' entry in a Cisco router's IP routing table?
explanation: The Gateway of Last Resort specifies the default route used to forward packets when no specific route matches the destination IP address in the routing table.

It is the loopback interface used strictly for TFTP firmware downloads

stem: Which DNS resource record type maps a human-readable hostname (e.g. www.cisco.com) to a 32-bit IPv4 address?

choices.text: A record
AAAA record
CNAME record
PTR record

stem: What is the primary function of a DNS Start of Authority (SOA) record?
explanation: The SOA record defines the core parameters of a DNS zone, including the primary authoritative master name server, administrator email, serial number, and zone transfer refresh/retry/expire timers.

Specifies the mail server priority for incoming email
Creates a temporary cryptographic token for DNSSEC verification

stem: What is 'Split Tunneling' in a remote access VPN deployment?
explanation: Split Tunneling directs corporate intranet traffic through the encrypted VPN tunnel, while public internet browsing traffic bypasses the VPN and exits directly through the user's local ISP connection.

choices.text: Routes corporate internal traffic through the encrypted VPN tunnel while general internet traffic exits directly via the user's local ISP

stem: What major security advantage does a 'Full Tunnel' VPN configuration offer over Split Tunneling in enterprise remote access deployments?
explanation: In a Full Tunnel, ALL client traffic (including general web browsing) is routed through the central corporate VPN gateway, ensuring that all traffic is subject to corporate firewalls, intrusion prevention, and web content filtering.

choices.text: All client traffic is forced through the corporate gateway, allowing full firewall inspection, DLP, and content filtering
It doubles client internet bandwidth speeds

explanation: IPsec ESP supports Transport mode (which encrypts only the payload and preserves the original IP header, used host-to-host) and Tunnel mode (which encrypts the entire original IP packet and adds a new IP header, used gateway-to-gateway).

choices.text: Transport mode and Tunnel mode
Symmetric mode and Asymmetric mode
Access mode and Trunk mode
Client mode and Server mode

stem: Which IPsec mode is standardly utilized for site-to-site VPN tunnels interconnecting two branch office gateways across the public Internet?
explanation: Tunnel mode is standard for site-to-site VPNs because it encapsulates and encrypts the entire private packet (including private RFC 1918 source and destination IPs) inside a new routable public IP header.

Transport mode
Promiscuous mode
Transparent mode

stem: What specific network attack is mitigated by enabling IPv6 Router Advertisement (RA) Guard on access switch ports?
explanation: IPv6 RA Guard blocks rogue routers or compromised hosts from sending unauthorized ICMPv6 Router Advertisements, preventing them from tricking clients into using a rogue gateway (Man-in-the-Middle) or bogus prefix.

choices.text: Rogue router attacks advertising unauthorized default gateways or false IPv6 prefixes
CAM table MAC address flooding attacks
DHCP starvation attacks on IPv4 access ports
CDP spoofing attacks by rogue VoIP phones

stem: What is a 'DHCP Starvation Attack' in Layer 2 security, and what attack tool is commonly used to execute it?
explanation: In a DHCP Starvation attack, an attacker uses a tool (such as Yersinia or Gobbler) to rapidly broadcast thousands of DHCPDISCOVER requests with spoofed MAC addresses, exhausting the DHCP server's available IP address pool and denying service to legitimate clients.

stem: In Layer 2 security, what is an 802.1Q 'Double-Tagging' VLAN hopping attack, and why must the attacker's switch port be in the Native VLAN?
explanation: In double-tagging, the attacker sends a frame with two 802.1Q tags. When the switch forwards it across a trunk, it strips the outer native tag without retagging (native VLAN behavior). The receiving switch reads the inner tag and forwards the frame into the target victim VLAN.

stem: When an enterprise NTP client receives time synchronization packets from a Stratum 1 server, what Stratum level does that client become if it serves time to downstream LAN devices?

choices.text: Stratum 2
Stratum 0
Stratum 1
Stratum 16

stem: What Layer 4 mechanism does Port Address Translation (PAT / NAT Overload) use to map hundreds of private internal IP addresses to a single public IP address?

choices.text: Unique source Layer 4 TCP and UDP port numbers
Unique 48-bit MAC addresses
802.1Q VLAN tag headers
IP TTL hop count decrements

stem: Which standard command-line network diagnostic tool is commonly used on Linux and Windows systems to test and query DNS name resolution?

netsh
tracert
ipconfig /flushdns
